# Bakamo

> Bakamo is a social intelligence company. Bakamo surfaces Social Truth by reading unprompted online conversation, then builds the quantitative instruments that measure it. The Reading Machine, Bakamo's proprietary technology, holds entire conversations at once; Bakamo's analysts interpret what they mean.

Founded 2016 (work began in 2014). Offices in New Jersey, London, Dortmund, Budapest and Kuala Lumpur. Founder & CEO: Daniel Fazekas. Contact: info@bakamosocial.com. Book a demo: https://www.bakamosocial.com/contact#book-a-demo.

## Research

- [Research](https://www.bakamosocial.com/research): Bakamo's public studies in one place, plus the Atlas of Social Truths as readable text
- [French Election Social Media Landscape Report 2017](https://www.bakamosocial.com/research/french-election-2017): summary of the 2017 report, with key facts, headline findings and a suggested citation
- [Hungarian election 2026 psychographic analysis](https://www.bakamosocial.com/elections): inner- and outer-directed discourse among Tisza and Fidesz supporters before the 12 April 2026 parliamentary election
- [Migration research](https://www.bakamosocial.com/migration): a decade of studies on how Europeans talk about migration, for foundations and policy institutions
- [French presidential election 2017 report (PDF)](https://www.bakamosocial.com/frenchelection): Bakamo's 2017 study of the French presidential election on social media

## Insights

- [Insights](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog): methodology and analysis articles
- [Cul-de-Sac vs. Inspiration Highway](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/cul-de-sac-vs-inspiration-highway): why the Reading Machine's vector space is deliberately "stupid", and the constructivist view of qual behind it (Daniel Fazekas, 2026)
- [Making Mushy Qual Mathematical](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/making-mushy-qual-mathematical): how vector maths gives qualitative research a map of the whole discourse, and makes saturation observable (Daniel Fazekas, 2026)
- [The Cost of Waiting](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/the-cost-of-waiting): the Reading Machine's energy use, why idle servers were the main cost, and the zero-idle architecture (Daniel Fazekas, 2026)
- [Human Truths Beneath the Numbers](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/human-truths-beneath-the-numbers): social truth explained, from a European Parliament talk on the Hungarian election call (Daniel Fazekas, 2026)
- [Progress or Regress: Where Is Qual Going?](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/progress-or-regress-where-is-qual-going): notes from QUAL360 on social listening vs. social intelligence and the case for a qualitative minimum (Daniel Fazekas, 2025)
- [Citizen Insights and EU Policymaking](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/citizen-insights-and-eu-policymaking): listen before you survey; Bakamo's public-sector cases at the ESOMAR Citizen Insights Summit (Daniel Fazekas, 2025)
- [Are Surveys Rigged Against Truth?](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/are-surveys-rigged-against-truth): how questionnaires frame their own answers, and the ESOMAR CEO survey story (Daniel Fazekas, 2024)
- [Why Negativity Is Great for Insight](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/why-negativity-is-great-for-insight): inverting complaints to find expectations; cautions on sentiment scores (Daniel Fazekas, 2024)
- [Boring AI vs. Exciting Humans](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/boring-ai-vs-exciting-humans): notes from IIeX on tools outshining research's mission (Daniel Fazekas, 2024)
- [TensionScope: Decoding the Human "Why" Behind the Data](https://www.bakamosocial.com/blog/tensionscope-decoding-the-human-why): the seven tensions framework (Team Bakamo, 2026)
